summary: Martin Peretz, born in 1938, is an American former magazine publisher and former Harvard University assistant professor. He bought The New Republic in 1974 and took editorial control in 1975 after firing its editor. Under him the magazine took liberal positions at home and pro-Israel, hawkish positions on foreign affairs, and he led it as editor-in-chief for decades. In 1996 he co-founded the financial news site TheStreet.com with Jim Cramer. He sold most of his stake in the magazine in 2002 and the rest in 2007, then bought it back with investors in 2009. He no longer has any association with it. Critics accused him of using the magazine to attack people he disagreed with, and of bigoted remarks about Arabs and Muslims. After a 2010 post saying "Muslim life is cheap", he apologised, and Harvard cancelled a planned speech by him.
